Pull request description:

  Part of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36692 (previously discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35994): replace procedural, field-by-field construction of `COutPoint`, `CTxIn` and `CTxOut` in test code with constructor calls.

  This PR covers cases that are context-dependent and need manual changes, independent of a scripted-diff for the trivial bulk:
  - `test/util/transaction_utils`: in `BuildSpendingTransaction`, the `scriptWitness` assignment has to be moved after `vin` is replaced, otherwise the witness is dropped.
  - `test/util/mining`: in `CreateBlockChain`, the coinbase input's fields were split by the output assignments, with comments that are now kept next to the constructor arguments.
  - `sigopcount_tests`: `BuildTxs` has the same witness ordering issue as `BuildSpendingTransaction`.
  - `bench/ccoins_caching`: The `scriptSig`s are built with `<<` appends, and the second output was created by `vout.resize(2)` but never assigned, so it is kept as a null `CTxOut{}`.
  - `transaction_tests`: `test_Get` builds the same transaction as `bench/ccoins_caching`, with the same `<<` appends and null second output.

  **This change is test- and bench-only and does not change the constructed transactions.**

  Notes for reviewers:
  - `CTxIn` has no witness constructor argument, so `scriptWitness` is assigned after `vin` is replaced.
  - `BuildTxs` is called repeatedly on the same transaction objects. Previously, `resize(1)` kept the existing inputs and only overwrote some of their fields; now they are replaced entirely. The fields that were left untouched by `BuildTxs` are never modified by the test, so the transactions are unchanged.
  - The null second output in `ccoins_caching` is copied from `test_Get` in `transaction_tests` and looks like an oversight. It is kept here to avoid behaviour changes.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36682: refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if

fa87bfe31dfda2d102c4e0cb5d39813cf84c7d1e refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if over iterator-based erase (MarcoFalke)
fa93a02563145aca3f96badaabe302b2dfa331d5 refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if over list removal or vector erase-remove (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  Convert `remove` and `remove_if` to the C++20 `std::erase` and `std::erase_if` overloads.

  The legacy ones can be confusing, because:

  * Array-based containers (like vector) must use the erase-remove idiom. Forgetting the erase, or forgetting to pass the end iterator (`bugprone-inaccurate-erase`) can be a bug, see also https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36588#discussion_r4345799022. So a call only to "remove" will not erase.
  * Node-based containers (like list or set) must not use the idiom. Using it will be a pessimization or won't compile. And correctly not using the idiom reads confusing, because a call to "remove" will actually erase.
  * They are more verbose.

  Also convert simple iterator-erase (which is verbose, but fine) to the std overload.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35714: validation: return block-file flush errors

12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056 validation: return block-file flush errors (Lőrinc)
07d23eb75527b8dd6571a33b3bc304815764bc07 test: characterize writes after flush failure (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** When flushing block or undo data fails, `FlushStateToDisk()` still writes block-index metadata and coins data, then advances `m_last_flushed_block`.
  With a separate `-blocksdir`, persistent failures there can leave metadata referring to block data that is not durable even when chainstate writes succeed.

  **Fix:** Return the flush error before those writes, leaving the last-flushed marker and on-disk coins tip unchanged in the failing call.
  Later flushes can retry and write if they succeed, including during shutdown.
  `ConnectTip()` and `DisconnectTip()` propagate the error before updating the chain tip, after applying the coins changes in memory.

  **History:**
  * [#27866](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27866#discussion_r1297313148) raised whether saving other state after a flush failure was preferable. This change preserves later retries while skipping writes in the failing call.
  * [#34897](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34897) introduced `m_last_flushed_block` to prevent persistent indexes from advancing past flushed chainstate. This fix keeps it at the last successful flush.

07d23eb75527b8dd6571a33b3bc304815764bc07 test: characterize writes after flush failure (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** When flushing block or undo data fails, `FlushStateToDisk()` still writes block-index metadata and coins data, then advances `m_last_flushed_block`.
  With a separate `-blocksdir`, persistent failures there can leave metadata referring to block data that is not durable even when chainstate writes succeed.

  **Fix:** Return the flush error before those writes, leaving the last-flushed marker and on-disk coins tip unchanged in the failing call.
  Later flushes can retry and write if they succeed, including during shutdown.
  `ConnectTip()` and `DisconnectTip()` propagate the error before updating the chain tip, after applying the coins changes in memory.

  **History:**
  * [#27866](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27866#discussion_r1297313148) raised whether saving other state after a flush failure was preferable. This change preserves later retries while skipping writes in the failing call.
  * [#34897](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34897) introduced `m_last_flushed_block` to prevent persistent indexes from advancing past flushed chainstate. This fix keeps it at the last successful flush.

  `BlockManager::AddToBlockIndex` only replaces best_header when the new header has strictly more chain work. Add a unit test that adds two sibling headers with equal work and checks that best_header keeps pointing to the first one.

  ```diff
  @@ -246,7 +246,7 @@ CBlockIndex* BlockManager::AddToBlockIndex(const CBlockHeader& block, CBlockInde
       pindexNew->nTimeMax = (pindexNew->pprev ? std::max(pindexNew->pprev->nTimeMax, pindexNew->nTime) : pindexNew->nTime);
       pindexNew->nChainWork = (pindexNew->pprev ? pindexNew->pprev->nChainWork : 0) + GetBlockProof(*pindexNew);
       pindexNew->RaiseValidity(BLOCK_VALID_TREE);
  -    if (best_header == nullptr || best_header->nChainWork < pindexNew->nChainWork) {
  +    if (best_header == nullptr || best_header->nChainWork <= pindexNew->nChainWork) {
           best_header = pindexNew;
       }
  ```

commit.message:
cli: fail to send a request when the socket does not become writable

HTTPClient::SendRequest() waits for the socket to become writable and
went back to waiting whenever Sock::Wait() returned without SendEvent.
Before 1805716354, the `continue` was the route to the deadline check. That
commit removed the deadline, so a Sock::Wait() timeout silently started
waiting again, forever. This means -rpcclienttimeout is never respected
when sending: bitcoin-cli will hang for as long as the server keeps the
connection open without reading the request.

Fix this by returning a failure whenever `Sock::Wait()` timeouts or errors.

  wallet_fundrawtransaction.py 11s -> 7s

  Wall 80s -> 75s

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36581: subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows

cf30d0a4123bb4237495f04e723ce9f706c2edf2 subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  `Popen::execute_process()` copied the command line into a buffer from `new[]`, but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows.

  `CreateProcessA` [needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa#:~:text=characters%2E-,The,violation) a writable command line buffer. Since C++17, `std::string::data()` supplies one, so give the `std::string` buffer directly and remove the copy.

  This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if `-signer=<cmd>` is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined `<cmd>`, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited.

  _edit: this was fixed upstream in https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/131, but since this codebase is C++20 it seems better to avoid the copy (and the const cast). A direct backport isn't possible anyway, since #35704 switched us to CreateProcessA._

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36465: Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests

5a4cd70547096af6247167d8dde6145a1b548642 Test: Add P2SH scriptSig stack-size boundary tests (benthecarman)

Pull request description:

  VerifyScript runs a P2SH scriptPubKey on the stack the scriptSig leaves before handling the redeemScript. The 20-byte push in HASH160 <20> EQUAL adds one item, so a scriptSig that leaves 1,000 items fails with STACK_SIZE, while 999 items is valid.

  An implementation that checks the redeemScript hash without running the scriptPubKey accepts the 1,000-item spend. No existing vector leaves the scriptSig at this boundary, so such an implementation can pass every row.

  Add 999 and 1,000 item cases with P2SH and WITNESS, and the 1,000 item case with no flags, which fails the same way because the scriptPubKey always runs. Also add the same boundary during redeemScript evaluation, where the restored stack plus the redeemScript's pushes reach 1,000 and 1,001 items.

  The same case is added as a feature_taproot spender in #36455, so its dump can be added to the script assets (bitcoin-core/qa-assets#297).

  These were discovered by finding gaps in an alternate implementation (rbitcoin)

fa0df9d336e80d37eab5f08b170a3255f287060c build: Bump Xcode CLT minimum supported version to 26.3 (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  Now that macOS 14 is EOL (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacOS_Sonoma), it seems odd to still support native Xcode CLT builds on it.

  (macOS Sonoma 14.8.9 received its final security update on 06 Aug 2026: https://support.apple.com/en-us/100100)

  This patch will only be released in version 33.x, another 6 months out from now. Also, depends builds (and thus release builds) are unaffected. Affected devs or users are free to build via brew, nix, etc...

  This is mostly needed to get an equivalent of llvm-19-ish via CLT, see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcode#Toolchain_versions. Specifically, it will allow to use C++20 CTAD and also allow switching the project to C++23.

5aaaf7b8d1ed72b7ab9eee117204f4c4346eb235 test: check network filtering and uniformity of addrman Select (Pieter Wuille)
9a0e095c687d7e139a9571883296cd9321e5beeb addrman: use uniform sampling inside buckets (Pieter Wuille)

Pull request description:

  The current way we sample from addresses within a bucket in addrman is randomized, but not perfectly random. It uses a linear scan, starting at a random position (out of the 64 positions in a bucket). This means that if for example only position 17 and 20 contain an address, 17 will be picked with probability 95.3% (whenever the initial position is 21..63 or 0..17) and 20 will be picked with probability 4.7% (whenever the initial position is 18..20).

  Make this search perfectly uniform, regardless of distribution of addresses within the bucket, by first copying all non-empty positions to a temporary array, and then selecting uniformly randomly from that array.

  Suggested by Crypt-iQ. Also pointed out earlier by mzumsande in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/23140#discussion_r733084509.

Pull request description:

  Clarify the message in case of assertion failures. Additionally unify the behavior of `NONFATAL_UNREACHABLE` w.r.t. abort handling.

  Motivation: This was discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34844#discussion_r3303436384

  The error message generated by `Assert`, `Assume`, and `CHECK_NONFATAL` contains the failing assertion condition text, but it's unclear whether that's the failed expectation or the actual case.

  For example,
  `"Internal bug detected: pindex != nullptr"`
  in fact means that what happened was `pindex == nullptr`.

  Clarify the situation, by inserting "\`%s\` check failed".

  The above example is now:
  ``"Internal bug detected: `pindex != nullptr` check failed"``
  which is more unambiguous.

  Additionally, change `NONFATAL_UNREACHABLE` to behave like `CHECK_NONFATAL`, and honor the special abort setting (`G_ABORT_ON_FAILED_ASSUME`).

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36559: test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex

2f7622e3f6f7ef431a7d5ec522958da62f33cec4 test: zero-pad the port in feature_anchors' expected hex (Kevin Ravensberg)

Pull request description:

  `feature_anchors.py` builds the expected `anchors.dat` substring from each peer's port with `hex(port)[2:]`, which is not zero-padded. The port is serialized as two bytes, so for ports below 4096 the expected string is one hex digit short and `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` fails.

  This only shows up with a non-default port range, for example when avoiding local listeners:

  ```
  TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100 test/functional/feature_anchors.py
  ```

  fails on master with `AssertionError` at the `assert ip_port in anchors_hex` line and passes with this change; the default range still passes.

  ---

flatfile: store position as a 64 bits integer

This is the last field that is only bounded by the usage callers make of it
(unlike the file number, for instance). Promoting it to a 64 bits integer also
does not change on-disk representation since we serialize positions as varints.
Therefore, widen them to prevent any possible future misuse.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36407: test: make orphanage_dos_many fill the orphanage

86ff13a0af0679ee0c725bac9c64c3e373cb0283 test: make orphanage_dos_many fill the orphanage (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  `test_orphanage_dos_many` checks that a normal peer's orphan survives while DoS peers flood the orphanage. I found that the orphanage never fills: the 60 peers send the same 51 orphans as `tx`, and a `tx` already held as an orphan is dropped in `ReceivedTx` without recording its sender. The orphanage peaks at 152 announcements against a limit of 3000, so nothing is evicted.

  Here the first peer sends the orphans and the other 59 announce them by `inv`, which does add them as announcers. The test now asserts that the orphanage holds 3000 announcements, instead of asserting on what it sends. It takes about as long as before.

  If `LimitOrphans` is changed to evict the normal peer's orphan first, the test used to pass and now fails. (`test_orphanage_dos_large` already catches that change.)

  Found while porting these tests to https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-node-tests.

  *Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36341: wallet: return error from bitcoin-wallet create

f64d33672fe1488b49254a634cbecfd9ce4ca179 wallet: return error from bitcoin-wallet create (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `bitcoin-wallet create` exits with status 0 even when the wallet couldn't be created:

  ```
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create   # first time, ok
  $ bitcoin-wallet -regtest -wallet=w1 create
  Failed to create database path '.../regtest/wallets/w1'. Database already exists.
  $ echo $?
  0
  ```

  In `ExecuteWalletToolFunc` the `create` branch only does something when `MakeWallet` succeeds and then falls through to `return true`. The other commands (`info`, `dump`, `createfromdump`) all return false on failure. So scripts that check the exit code think the wallet was created.

  This returns false when `MakeWallet` fails, the same way `info` does. The added check in `tool_wallet.py` runs `create` on the existing wallet `foo` and expects exit code 1. It fails on master (`not(0 == 1)`) and passes with the fix.
